images.filename: London downstream from Westminster Pier geograph-3071087-by-Ben-Brooksbank.jpg
images.caption:
View downstream from Westminster Pier - in 1958.
Hungerford Railway Bridge (with footbridge only on the downstream side) is prominent, as is the old Shot Tower still standing by the quite new Royal Festival Hall. Over to the right they are beginning to build the Shell Tower. In the distance St Paul's Cathedral seems to stand alone and between the cranes the new Bankside Power Station is just visible. Much else is yet to come in the next 50 years!
images.alt:

images.filename: Event Horizon, RFH and London Eye - geograph.org.uk - 452991.jpg
images.caption: Event Horizon: RFH and London Eye The life-size, life-like figures perched on the roof of the Royal Festival Hall are just two of around 30 that make up an outdoor installation by Antony Gormley on both sides of the Thames. There may be another at ground level but they are difficult to distinguish from the passers-by.

images.filename: "The Big Giving" by Klaus Weber - geograph.org.uk - 543564.jpg
images.caption: "The Big Giving" by Klaus Weber This year's Royal Festival Hall fountain project is "The Big Giving" by German artist Klaus Weber, situated on the Festival Terrace adjacent to the Golden Jubilee Bridge. It consists of six strange sculptures of heads and arms that rise out of volcanic-looking mounds of black rock with water gushing from mouths, eyes, ears and other orifices! (July-September 2007)
